title: Cloudflare Opens Quicksilver to Customers as Workers KV Instant, Inside a 1 MB Envelope
gist: Cloudflare exposed its internal Quicksilver config store to customers as Workers KV 'Instant' mode: 1.62 ms p99 reads and ~107 ms median global write replication, but capped at 1 MB/10,000 keys, one write per namespace per second, and priced steeply for writes and storage. Private beta, no GA date.

insights.claim: Cloudflare's KV Instant mode reads at 1.62 ms p99 versus 287 ms for classic Workers KV, measured to over 300 edge locations.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: A roughly 170x read-latency improvement makes edge config lookups effectively free on the request hot path.
insights.locator: The published figures, measured to over 300 edge locations

insights.claim: Write replication in KV Instant has a median of 107 ms and p99 of 256 ms, versus under 1 s median and 4.38 s p99 for classic KV, where the classic median and p95 are upper bounds because Cloudflare lacks sub-second fidelity there.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Near-instant global propagation enables flag flips and config changes without TTL waits.
insights.locator: Cloudflare notes it has no sub-second fidelity

insights.claim: Quicksilver is Cloudflare's own configuration store from 2020, consulted by nearly every request to Cloudflare, and had never been a customer-facing product before KV Instant.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Productizing a proven internal system signals Cloudflare is monetizing core infrastructure for developers.
insights.locator: Quicksilver is Cloudflare's own configuration store

insights.claim: A KV Instant namespace holds at most 10,000 key-value pairs and 1 MB total, with keys up to 300 bytes, and mode cannot be changed after namespace creation.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Hard size caps limit it to small config data, not general-purpose KV workloads.

insights.claim: KV Instant caps writes at one per namespace per second, versus one write per key per second in classic KV, so a pattern classic KV permits across many keys concurrently becomes a single serialised queue when migrating.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: The migration gotcha most likely to bite teams; write-heavy workloads must stay on classic KV.
insights.locator: Writes are capped at one per namespace per second

insights.claim: KV Instant pricing is $0.20 per million reads (60% below classic's $0.50), $0.10 per write operation against $5.00 per million in classic, and $100 per MB per month storage versus $0.50 per GB.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Pricing explicitly steers usage to read-often, write-rarely data; write costs are ~20,000x classic per operation.

insights.claim: Cloudflare itself states that for KV Instant 'storage and Class A operations are significantly more expensive than Workers KV', consistent with a store priced for constant reads and rare writes.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Treat it as a premium hot-path config tier, not a cheaper KV.
insights.quote: storage and Class A operations are significantly more expensive than Workers KV

insights.claim: Feature flags, routing tables and agent settings fit KV Instant's small, read-heavy, rarely-updated shape, while session state, user records and anything with a write path do not.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Use as a decision rule for what to move to Instant versus classic KV.
insights.locator: Feature flags, routing tables and agent settings fit that shape.

insights.claim: Practitioners compared KV Instant to Vercel Global Config, with one developer citing Vercel's claimed 15 ms middleware reads; Cloudflare's reply was that even classic KV's p50 two years ago was about 5 ms and Instant is faster.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Edge config latency is becoming a competitive axis between Cloudflare and Vercel.
insights.locator: The comparison practitioners reached for was Vercel.

insights.claim: Classic Workers KV, launched in 2018, remains Cloudflare's recommendation for large or frequently updated data, so the two modes now sit under one API with opposite economics.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Cloudflare is segmenting one API into read-optimised and write-optimised pricing tiers.
insights.locator: Classic Workers KV, which launched during Birthday Week

insights.claim: KV Instant is in private beta behind a sign-up form; Cloudflare plans a wider opening but gives no general availability date.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: No production commitment yet; track beta expansion and GA announcement.
insights.locator: KV Instant is in private beta
